description: On a real `git commit` (detected from the PARSED argv — not `git stash`/`worktree`/`status`, not a `commit` token in a comment/message/pathspec/sibling), checks that an AI code review ran this session (a marker file touched by the review tool). If none ran, blocks with a reminder to run review on the uncommitted diff first. Skips: a DOCS-ONLY staged diff (every path a doc extension *.md/*.mdx/*.rst/*.adoc, or a NON-code file under docs/ — source/script/config like *.py/docs/conf.py/docs/Makefile never counts, a bare *.txt counts only under docs/; and only for a plain commit — not `-a`/`-p`/pathspec/`--pathspec-from-file`/`--git-dir`/`GIT_DIR=`). There is NO self-service skip (the old `REVIEW_SKIP=1` inline env and `[skip-review: <reason>]` trailer are removed, deny-by-default); a one-time exception is an external Telegram approval requested via RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_REQUIRE_REVIEW_BEFORE_COMMIT="<why>" (deny-by-default; bare `1` rejected). The `git diff --cached` lister is timeout-bounded; on failure it forfeits the docs-only fast-path (the marker gate still runs — NOT an allow). timeout_ms 960000 STRICTLY EXCEEDS the hatch helper's 930s worst case (tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus a 30s cleanup margin): with the hatch requested, a hung/unanswered tg-ctl must resolve to the helper's own deny BEFORE the bridge's descriptor-timeout kill — otherwise on_error=open would race that kill into a SILENT ALLOW, re-opening the exact self-service bypass this conversion closes. Claude Code settings entries that launch cc_hook_bridge must also set timeout >960s (the CC command-hook default 600s will preempt this descriptor). The common env-unset deny path may make ONE bounded daemon-local grant pull (tg-ctl ask --verify-grant --pull, agent-tools#742; ~20s worst case: 15s lookup cap + a git rev-parse for repoRoot) before denying, once per (hook, cwd) per process — fail-closed, no Telegram card. on_error=open: process-discipline gate, not a security gate — a crash should warn, not wedge committing.
